title: Effect of amlodipine on morbidity and mortality in severe chronic heart failure
authors: Packer M, O'Connor CM, Ghali JK, Pressler ML, Carson PE, Belkin RN, et al.; Prospective Randomized Amlodipine Survival Evaluation Study Group
population: Patients with severe chronic heart failure and ejection fraction below 30% on usual therapy, stratified by ischaemic or non-ischaemic cause
funder: Supported by a grant from Pfizer Central Research. One author (A.B.C.) is listed at Pfizer Central Research, Groton, Connecticut.
result: Double-blind amlodipine (n=571) against placebo (n=582). The primary end point of death from any cause or hospitalisation for major cardiovascular events occurred in 39% against 42% (9% risk reduction, 95% CI 24% reduction to 10% increase, P=0.31); death in 33% against 38% (16% reduction, 31% reduction to 2% increase, P=0.07). In non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy amlodipine reduced the combined risk by 31% (P=0.04) and death by 46% (P<0.001); no difference in ischaemic heart disease. Peripheral oedema (P<0.001) and pulmonary oedema (P=0.01) occurred more often with amlodipine, the authors putting the risk of pulmonary oedema attributable to amlodipine at 5 percent; worsening renal function 7.7% against 3.6% (P=0.002). Hospitalisation for worsening heart failure 36% against 39%. The authors propose dilatation of pulmonary arterioles, rather than an adverse effect on the heart, as the cause of the pulmonary oedema.
